principles: A single 401, 403, 404, 5xx, novel IP or novel path is not hostile evidence by itself.
GET and HEAD to established public routes are usually normal-like when behavior matches baseline.
POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE are context-dependent and must not be treated as suspicious merely because they mutate state.
Known recurring application/API/static routes can become scoped normal baselines from repeated evidence.
Secret, backup, framework-admin and configuration probes contribute suspicious evidence when combined with breadth, repetition or correlation.
Distributed low-rate activity may form a campaign hypothesis only from behavioral correlation, never subnet membership alone.
Unknown means uncertain; uncertainty must not be silently converted into normal or malicious.
privacy: Persist normalized path without query string; never learn request bodies, credentials, tokens or query values.
